THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS 
127 Drummond Street 


Montreal 


the Young Men’s Christian Association of Montreal, 

the Sixty-Ninth Annual Report of your Board of Directors. 

All through the year just closed it has been evident to 
all keen observers that the foundation principles, motives, 
and methods of the Association must necessarily be tested 
and readjusted to the after-war conditions. It is also evident 
that we are in a critical period for our Nation and our Move- 
ment. The unrest in the industrial world, following the 
great war, has laid a heavier responsibility upon the Asso- 
ciation. 


I HAVE the honor to submit herewith, as Secretary of 


In looking over the year’s work, your Directors feel 
grateful to God for His presence and assistance in bringing 
to our buildings such great numbers of young men and boys. 
Many were the temptations and trials that assailed them, 
and here they found help and assistance. We enter, there- 
fore, upon a new year with confidence that the same Guiding 
Hand will ever be our strength and stay. 


This year our activities have been conducted through 
the following departments: the Metropolitan Board, directing, 
supervising and promoting the City-wide activities; the 
general work in the Branches; the non-equipment or com- 
munity extension work, placing the experience of the Asso- 
ciation at the disposal of the community agencies, the 
Churches, homes, schools, etc.; the industrial work, co- 
operating in the industries in the different parts of the City; 
the Senior and Junior Camps, providing healthy and con- 
structive rest and recreation for our men and boys; and the 
Red Triangle Hut on Dominion Square, serving the returned 
soldiers. 


In these different departments the work has been carried 
on by 1182 volunteer men serving on Committees, 28 em- 
ployed officers, and 87 general employees, and many others 
who have associated their efforts for the moral and religious 
welfare of the men and boys of our City. 


1 


The total membership in good standing at the end of the 
Association year was 6,784, which does not include free 
memberships issued to returned soldiers good for six months. 
Classified by Branches, we have in Central Branch 3,294 
Seniors and 729 Juniors; in Westmount Branch, 318 Seniors 
and 315 Juniors; in North Branch, 472 Seniors and 306 
Juniors; in Railroad Branch, 1,165 Seniors and 185 Juniors. 

Your Board of Directors in supervising and directing 
the work through the year have continuously had in mind 
the interests of the whole City, and have endeavored to meet 
the needs of the different sections as revealed through in- 
tensive studies conducted by our Community Committee. 


We are pleased to report that during the year the most 
cordial relationships have existed between the Churches and 
the Association, our Secretaries co-operating with the Inter- 
Church Survey Committee. Mr. John Bradford is Chairman 
of the General City Committee which has charge of the work. 
Mr. Swetman, of the Central Branch, is Secretary of the 
Central District Committee, and the Association in every 
way is seeking to co-operate. 


Finance—During the year a Joint Financial Campaign 
was held for the National and Local Y.M.C.A. and Y.W.C.A. 
current expenses. We have been able to live within our 
budget. Although the introduction of our industrial activity 
through the community extension work has added materially 
to the budget, it has been fully met by special subscriptions 
and by checking other avenues of expenditure. Every 
Branch by careful management and strict economy has 
been able to close the year with a small balance on the right 
side. During the year $1,300.00 has been received in 
legacies. The total receipts from all sources for the Asso- 
ciation year amounted to $153,021.79. The excess in ex- 
penditures over receipts from fees, etc., was provided for 
by our Red Triangle Financial Campaign held in May last, 
and amounted to $63,058.98. 

Owing to the Grand Trunk Railway removing their 
roundhouse to Turcot some years ago, our Railroad Branch 
in Point St. Charles did not meet the needs of the locality 
as had been expected. On March 15th last, your Directors, 


3 


with the consent of the active membership of the Association, 
sold our building there to the Grand Trunk Railway Com- 
pany. A building more centrally located on lots owned by 
the Association on Wellington Street will more adequately 
serve the needs of Point St. Charles and Verdun. 

A strong City-wide Building Committee has been formed 
to study the need for buildings in the different parts of the 
City. It is evident that a building must be placed, in the 
very near future, in Point St. Charles to take care of our 
membership there. ‘The claims of other sections are also 
becoming very insistent. 

During the year we have issued 4,991 free memberships 
to returned men, which entitled them to all the advantages 
of the Association for a period of six months. ‘The attendance 
at all the Association buildings in the City for the year has 
been over 338,104. 

Reuticious Worx—For a number of years the Montreal 
Association has assisted in the support of Mr. C. S. Paterson 
in India by undertaking a portion of his budget, which in 
1918 amounted to $1,658.00. This year it was felt that this 
amount should be greatly increased. A strong Foreign 
Work Committee, under the leadership of Mr. William 
Currie, was organized, composed of members from each 
Branch. Meetings were held once a month, which were 
addressed by Foreign Work speakers. I am glad to report 
that the subscriptions were increased from $1,658.00 to 
$3,000.00. Next year we are aiming to increase this amount 
by fifty per cent, making our objective $4,500.00. This is, 
of course, in addition to the large subscriptions of individual 
friends and members. 

On Sunday afternoons inspirational meetings have 
been held. Prof. Ritchie, together with Dr. Symonds, 
Canon Shatford, Dr. Hanson, and Rev. Geo. Adam, gave 
strong addresses. 

Bible Classes and Bible Study Groups were organized, 
resulting in bringing together many of our young men. 

In the Boys’ Department, also, were organized Life 
Problem groups, practical talks, and club meetings, led by 
men of deep Christian conviction. Personal interviews were 


3 


arranged which no doubt have been a factor in the number 
of our boys joining the Church this Spring. ‘Talks were 
given to the clubs on Church membership. During Easter, 
Week strong emphasis was laid on the necessity of joining 
the Church. 

A business men’s noonday prayer meeting has been 
organized in Central Branch, meeting at 12.30 for one-half 
hour on Wednesday of each week. 

The social life of our young men and boys has not been 
overlooked. It is realized that too often this side of a young 
man’s life is neglected and he drifts from the high ideals he 
set up for himself when he left home to pursue his studies 
or his fortune in a great City. Concerts, social evenings, 
skating and snowshoeing parties have been arranged and 
have proved very beneficial. 

The Physical Departments of the Branches have em- 
phasized the great need of better physical development, and 
have set up, under the leadership of fully trained Physical 
Directors, a programme designed to meet the needs of all 
the membership. During the year 72,221 men and boys 
have taken physical training. 

The Educational Work has been of a high order. While 
it is of necessity conducted at a loss to the Association, yet 
we have through this department been able to reach and 
help many young men and boys by day and evening classes 
who could never otherwise have received the qualifications 
for deserved promotion in their employment. 

During the year the community or non-equipment 
extension work of the Association has been successfully 
promoted. The great need of some form of Association 
work in the less favored districts of the City where no Asso- 
ciation buildings are yet placed has been keenly felt, and to 
meet this need a Community Secretary has been placed in 
each of the following districts; Maisonneuve, Verdun, and 
Point St. Charles, to co-operate with the Churches, the 
schools, and other agencies in providing, as far as possible, 
the advantages of a regular Association building; and by a 
careful study of the whole situation, placing the facts of 
community life and needs before all the constructive agencies, 


4 


utilizing the present equipment and securing new where 
necessary, training leaders, organizing physical classes, 
athletics, Sunday School groups, conferences, and taking 
part in all movements for community betterment. 


The Red Triangle Hut is to be carried on as a community 
activity under the control of Central Board of Management 
for this year. 

A trained Secretary will be placed June Ist. next inthe 
district East of Bleury Street, South of Ontario, to work 
among the under-privileged boys. 

At our Annual Meeting in May last, one of the recom- 
mendations adopted was that we should seriously undertake 
a definite industrial programme. Seventy-five per cent of 
the men in Montreal are industrial workers. They must 
be served. In the Fall, therefore, your Board decided to 
interview the leaders of industry in Cote St. Paul and 
Maisonneuve, finding in each locality many firms who were 
willing to consider the introduction of Association work in 
their factories. 


Captain J. Morley Carson, who was formerly General 
Secretary at Westmount Branch, was secured to work in the 
industries in Cote St. Paul; and Captain James Clarke, in 
Maisonneuve. In these two districts we are working in 
twelve industries which employ over 8,000 men. Two 
hundred and sixty-eight men and boys are serving on Com- 
mittees. The work was warmly welcomed by the men in 
the industries and is proving successful. 


In the past years the Senior and Junior Camps have 
proved a splendid asset to the work of the Association, our 
Secretaries getting into intimate relationships with the boys 
and men, understanding their individual personalities, which 
aided materially in securing their co-operation and loyal 
support in the work of building up Christian character. 

During the year the Junior Camp was operated from 
June 25th to August 26th with an attendance of 289 boys, 
the operations showing a small balance on the right side. 
The accommodations, however, were very crowded. At 
one time there were as many as 165 boys, while the Camp 
cannot comfortably accommodate more than 80 or 90. 


5 


The great need of extending the Camp to accomodate a 
larger number was felt by your Board. Figures were obtained 
by the Permanent Camp Committee as to the cost of the 
improvements. Included in the budget of 1920 is a sum 
sufficient to enlarge the Camp to accommodate 200 boys. 
The Junior Camp Committee has been charged with the 
erection of a new dining pavilion and other buildings necessary. 
This work is well advanced at the present time and will be 
in readiness for the opening of the Camp this year.. Mr. 
MacKinnon has been appointed Director for this season, 
and has been successful in securing splendid assistants. 


The Senior Camp Committee has been entirely re- 
organized and is pushing its plans vigorously. Mr. Herb 
Patterson has been released to take charge. Last year we 
had a total attendance of 106 men. The receipts also showed 
a small balance to the credit of the Camp. 


Your Acting Secretary attended the Annual Meeting 
and Convention of the National Council in Toronto, January 
20th to 22nd; also the International Convention in Detroit, 
where over 4,000 Secretaries and Association men attended. 
He also attended the Metropolitan Secretaries’ Conference 
held in Washington in February, where the larger problems 
of the Association were considered and a constructive pro- 
gramme for extension work of the Association was formulated. 
These conferences have been of great help in the year’s work. 


Starr Cuancrs—Central Branch—Mr. W. H. Hen- 
derson, Executive Secretary, resigned in September to take 
the Executive Secretaryship at Halifax. He was succeeded 
by Major J. W. Beaton on November Ist. Capt. H. C. 
Patterson joined the staff as Secretary of the Young Men’s 
Section in July and resigned April 30th to accept the position 
of Physical Director in Westmount Branch. Mr. R. Ingleson 
joined the staff on August Ist as Membership Secretary. 
Mr. H. J. Swetman, as Service Secretary, joined in February. 
During the year Mr. E. T. Armitage and Mr. Hay Finlay 
joined the Boys’ Department staff. Mr. A. H. Duesberry, 
as Assistant Physical Director, joined in September Ist. 
Mr. D. Stewart resigned to attend McGill College. 


6 


Westmount—Capt. T. Hicks Miller joined the staff on 
August Ist as Secretary for the Men’s Section, and Mr. 
A. D. Youmans resigned May Ist, 1920, to accept the position 
of Physical Director at Brandon, Man. 


NorthBranch—Mr.J.G.Cruickshank, resigned April 30th 
from the Boys’ Secretaryship to enter business. 


Your Directors wish to express their appreciation of 
the splendid leadership and assistance given by the Board 
of Management, the Ladies’ Auxiliary, the volunteer workers, 
and the employed officers of each Branch; also the Military 
Committee of the Red Triangle Hut, the Secretaries in charge, 
and the splendid self-sacrifice of the Ladies’ Military Com- 
mittee. 


We are sorry to have to record the following deaths 
among our subscribers during the year:— 


A. Baumgarten E. F. Hebden. 

Geo. Creak. Wn. P. Hunt. 

J. C. Holden. Hon. N. W. Trenholme. 
H. H. Lang. Richard I. Holland. 
Col. E. B. Busteed. Dr. Walter C. Bazin. 
Wm. Coristine. Judge A. G. Cross. 
Alfred J. Heath. J. Cochrane King. 

Miss Violet Brien. John Murphy. 

R. A. Becket. Dundan Gordon. 

Wm. Louis Haldimand. Donald S. Robertson. 


All of which is respectfully submitted, 


DR. F. D. ADAMS, 
President. 
J. O. LOUGH, 
Acting General Secretary. 


Montreat, May 12th, 1920.
